summary:
ORVEN is an educational space simulation video game that allows users to experience the process of designing, planning, and executing a space mission through engineering-based decisions. Through an interactive experience guided by two animated characters, Sam and Laika, players can choose missions with different difficulty levels, design their own spacecraft, and select components such as materials, propulsion systems, energy, communications, and landing systems, while considering their advantages, disadvantages, mass, and cost.

The game simulates different stages of a mission, from launch to arrival at the destination, incorporating variables such as altitude, distance, fuel consumption, environmental conditions, and resource availability. Every decision affects the outcome, allowing players to achieve successful, partially successful, or failed missions, each accompanied by an evaluation and feedback.

ORVEN aims to transform complex aerospace engineering concepts into an accessible, dynamic, and educational experience, bringing students closer to the real challenges of space exploration while encouraging critical thinking, creativity, and decision-making skills.
details:
ORVEN V5 is an advanced interactive simulation, design, and space mission management platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Its primary purpose is to bring aerospace engineering and interplanetary mission design closer to both students and space enthusiasts through an interactive, rigorous web environment grounded in real data.

1. What does it do and how does it work?

ORVEN V5 operates as an aerospace mission simulation and design environment within the browser. It enables users to:

  • Explore and configure space missions: Select trajectories and orbital targets (such as missions to the Moon, Mars, asteroids, or Galilean moons).
  • Build vehicles in an Interactive 3D Hangar: The system features an exhaustive catalog of real technical components (propellers, power systems, GNC avionics, structures, and tanks) based on official specifications from NASA and international space agencies.
  • Simulate flight scenarios and orbital trajectories: Allows real-time visualization of flight phases (liftoff, stage separation, atmosphere, orbit, and planetary insertion) while dynamically calculating masses, costs, energy budgets, and communication data rates.
  • Auditing and automatic scoring: Upon completing the design, the platform generates a detailed report evaluating technical viability, compliance with standards (such as NASA-STD-5001B and NASA-STD-5012B), and overall mission efficiency.

2. What benefits does it offer?

  • Interactive STEM education: Translates complex calculations of delta-v, dry/wet mass, TRL (Technology Readiness Level), and thermal budgets into an intuitive visual experience.
  • Accessible technical rigor: Incorporates real components (engines such as the SpaceX Raptor, RS-25, RL10, RTG generators, and autonomous navigation systems like AutoNav), allowing users to understand the real trade-offs faced by aerospace engineers.
  • Multiplatform accessibility: Being entirely implemented in standard web technologies, it does not require the installation of heavy or specialized software.

3. What is the expected impact?

The project aims to democratize space mission design, serving as a pedagogical resource in university and technical classrooms, as well as a tool for scientific outreach to inspire the next generation of engineers, scientists, and researchers within the framework of sustainable space exploration and Artemis missions.

4. Tools, languages, hardware, and software used

  • Frontend development and 3D graphics: Semantic HTML5, advanced CSS3 (with variables and responsive design adapted for desktop and mobile devices), and modern JavaScript (ES6+).
  • Graphic rendering engine: Implementation of an interactive 3D viewer based on HTML5 Canvas with support for 360° camera manipulation, zoom, and flight phase simulation.
  • Database and technical data: JSON structure integrated with over 250 aerospace components validated against public documentation from NASA, NTRS (NASA Technical Reports Server), JAXA, and ESA.

5. In what way is your project creative?

ORVEN V5 stands out by combining the analytical depth of aerospace engineering software with the visual design and user experience of a high-end modern mission-design game (editorial aerospace interface).

  • It integrates an interactive built-in virtual assistant (companion dock with dynamic avatars) that guides the user throughout mission design.
  • It fuses hyper-realistic technical data (NASA engineering standards, source traceability, and launch safety regulations) into a strategy and mission-design game.

6. What factors did the team take into account?

During the project's development, the following critical engineering factors were prioritized:

  • Fidelity and Traceability: Every catalog component features a direct reference to real technical standards (e.g., NASA-STD-5012B, AFSPCMAN 91-710) and links to public NASA sources.
  • Performance Optimization: Code structuring to ensure a stable frame rate in 3D rendering and smooth navigation between the various modules (Hangar, Agency, Flight, and Orbits).
  • Robustness and Error Handling: Cross-validation of mass constraints, payload capacities of selected launchers, and electrical power budgets.
